notes: The whole 60-page PDF, read end to end: the historical context, the architecture and architects chapters, the figure captions, the footnotes, the bibliography and the twenty-one-page Appendix I. The report is a survey of one block and a bit — the block bounded by Greenwich, Lombard, Larkin and Polk streets plus three buildings at the northwest corner of Lombard and Larkin, 30 properties holding 35 buildings — so its study-area facts are dense rather than numerous. Its architect biographies (pp. 33-38) carry a second, larger seam: about thirty numbered buildings elsewhere in the city, each with an architect and a date, which are recorded here too. Appendix I is entirely biographies of residents and is the reason the yield is not larger: facts whose only content is who lived at an address are not recorded, per the privacy limits in the root AGENTS.md. Two exceptions are taken under that file's allowance for notable past residents already covered by published sources — Gelett Burgess at 1210-1212 Lombard Street and Alice Eastwood at 1241 Lombard Street. Carpenters, builders and contractors are named in their building role, which the same rule permits; owners and occupants are not. Two things about this document govern how it must be read. First, the Larkin Street numbers in the study area were changed: the report prints an original number and, in the appendix, 'site of today's #', so the pre-renumbering numbers are historical and must never be looked up as current addresses. 2515 Larkin Street names two different buildings in this report for that reason. Second, the OCR is degraded throughout — 'Hil' for Hill, '80s and Quandt' for Boss and Quandt, '100 I Front Street' for 1001 Front Street — so street numbers were taken only where they read cleanly or are confirmed by a second mention.

coverage.remaining: Nothing in this document. The DPR 523 forms it says will be attached as an appendix are not in this file and are a separate document; so is the discussion of a potential historic district, which the report defers to a final draft. The Junior League's Here Today (1968) and its building files at the San Francisco History Center, the Corbett Heights Neighbors and other statements on the same SF Planning page, and Kostura's Argonaut article on San Francisco Italianates (the argonaut-sfhs source) are all separate and untouched.
coverage.note: Read all 60 pages. A mechanical scan of the text yields 298 numbered-address mentions, and a few more are hidden by OCR run-ons the scan cannot see ("100 I Front Street" for 1001 Front, "1205 Filbert2061 Hyde" for two addresses, "l2l2 Lombard" for 1212). They become 109 findings over 104 distinct addresses: 52 on the study-area blocks of Larkin, Lombard, Greenwich and Polk; 37 buildings elsewhere in the city named in the architect biographies; 19 premises elsewhere named in the appendix, mostly shops and firms; and the report's note of the Department of Building Inspection's own address, recorded only so a later run does not read it as a property. Ten printed addresses are not recorded at all: 1230 Vallejo Street, 915 Hyde Street, 1433 Greenwich Street, 1330 Lombard Street and 2638-2642 Larkin Street appear solely as somebody's home and are left out under the privacy limits; a house at Haight Avenue and Sixth Street is in Alameda, not San Francisco; and the Sing Chong and Sing Fat buildings at California and Grant, the First Baptist Church at Octavia and Market, the Odd Fellows Columbarium on Lorraine Court near Geary and Arguello, and the orphanage on Ocean Boulevard are given by cross street with no number, which under the evidence bar is not an address.
